title: People in Iceland say NO to the EU

paragraphs: Icelanders have voted against resuming membership talks with the EU in a national referendum. With almost all votes counted, 52.5% of voters rejected the government’s proposal to restart negotiations, while 47.5% supported it.

Prime Minister’s government had brought the vote forward due to global geopolitical tensions; however, international issues didn’t dominate the debate. Political experts explained that the NO campaign successfully focused on domestic identity, national independence, and protecting Iceland’s fishing waters. In contrast, the YES campaign ran a very technical campaign that failed to excite the public.

Even though the referendum was only about reopening preliminary discussions rather than deciding on actual EU membership, voters chose to protect their sovereignty. This result stops Iceland’s path toward joining the EU for the near future.

paragraphs: People in Iceland voted No in a referendum about the EU. They decided not to restart talks about joining the EU.

About 52.5% of people voted No, and 47.5% voted Yes. The Prime Minister wanted to hold the vote earlier because of global problems, but the political debate stayed focused on local issues. Many Icelanders wanted to protect their national independence and their fishing waters.

Political experts said that the NO group made a strong campaign about identity and feelings. The YES group only talked about technical details, so they couldn’t convince enough people. As a result, Iceland will remain outside the European Union.

paragraphs: Iceland has a big vote about the European Union. Most people vote No. They do not want to talk about joining the EU.

About 52.5% vote No and 47.5% voted Yes. Icelanders want to stay independent. They also want to protect their fish and waters. Fewer people say Yes because the NO group does not have interesting ideas. The government wants to start new talks, but the people say no. Iceland will not join the European Union now.
